cross validation

Giuliana Motta

2026-11-17

Cross validation

Randomly split you data into training and testing - The training data you use to build your model - Testing is date you use to evaluate out of dampl fit - Exact ratio depends on data sixe, but I like 80/20 - Evaluate using the root mean squared error (compute it only in the testing data set) - What a higher RMSE

Repeat the partition a couple of times You can fold (5-fold is where the data is split into 5 parts. One is training and the other 4 are test)

Comes up a lot in modern methods - variable selection (lasso) - most of the time you don’t really get p-values, you focus on prediction accuracy instead - its because the goals are usually different for these types of analysis.

Coding

load in packages

library(tidyverse)

library(modelr)
library(mgcv)
## Loading required package: nlme
## 
## Attaching package: 'nlme'
## 
## The following object is masked from 'package:dplyr':
## 
##     collapse
## 
## This is mgcv 1.9-4. For overview type '?mgcv'.
library(p8105.datasets)

Lidar data

data("lidar")

lidar_df =
  lidar |> 
  mutate(id = row_number()) |> 
  select(id, everything()) #this reoders things to put id in the front

lidar_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x= range, y = logratio)) +
  geom_point()

Build training and testing datasets - sample at random your training data set

train_df = sample_frac(lidar_df, size = .8)
test_df = anti_join(lidar_df, train_df, by = "id") #of everything in one thing, what is not in the other
ggplot(train_df, aes(x = range, y = logratio)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_point(data = test_df, color = "red") #you can see where the testing data set in red

Fit some models

linear_mod = lm(logratio ~ range, data = train_df)
smooth_mod = mgcv::gam(logratio ~ s(range), data = train_df) #gam stands for generalized additive models, s stands for a smooth fit, but gam does still assume constant variance - Jeff hates cubic polynomials lol 
wiggly_mod = mgcv::gam(logratio ~ s(range, k = 30), sp = 10e-6, data = train_df) #this happens when you add a number of breaks

make a plot

train_df |> 
  add_predictions(wiggly_mod) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = range, y = logratio)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line(aes(y = pred), color = "red")

do model comparisons

rmse(linear_mod, test_df)
## [1] 0.121005
rmse(smooth_mod, test_df)
## [1] 0.06636809
rmse(wiggly_mod, test_df)
## [1] 0.0749454
